info.title: Emmy Platform API Documentation
info.description:
# Introduction

Integrate your agency's systems with the Emmy platform. This reference currently
covers the Tokenized Link API (v1 and v2) for creating personalized reporting links and the
CE Activity Report webhook for outbound community engagement reports. Find the
webhook under **Receiving data from the Emmy Platform**, including its JSON
request example, signing headers, expected response, and signed cURL sample.
Its component models include self-attested employment, validated payroll, and education.
Your agency hosts this receiver.
Examples use synthetic applicant data and nonfunctional tokens.

Object schemas allow additional properties for forward compatibility. Integrations
should tolerate unknown response fields so new fields can be added without breaking
existing clients. Required fields and documented field types still apply.

<!-- Remove this link-check exception after the first reviewed deployment. -->
<!-- markdown-link-check-disable-next-line -->
[Download the official OpenAPI JSON](https://DSACMS.github.io/iv-cbv-payroll/openapi.json).
The JSON and this reference are generated together from executable API tests.

## API environments

| Environment | Base URL | Purpose |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Dev | https://verify-demo.navapbc.cloud | Develop and test integrations. |
| Demo | https://demo.reportmyincome.org | Demonstrate and evaluate the platform. |

These URLs host the invitation API. Report webhooks use your agency's configured
receiver URL instead.

Use HTTPS for every request and the API key issued for the selected environment.
Your production hostname and credentials are provided during agency onboarding.

## API keys and authentication

Contact [emmy@cms.hhs.gov](mailto:emmy@cms.hhs.gov) to request an agency API key
for each environment. The Tokenized Link API uses a 32-character secret API key.
Keep it on your server, never in browser code or public repositories.

For invitation requests, each key identifies an agency and its configured metadata and invitation settings.
Sending a `client_agency_id` cannot select another agency. Include these headers:

```http
Authorization: Bearer API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json
```

A missing or invalid key returns `401 Unauthorized` with the plain-text body
`HTTP Token: Access denied.` and a `WWW-Authenticate` header. If a key is
compromised, contact emmy@cms.hhs.gov to have it replaced.

Outbound report webhooks use HMAC signing headers instead of Bearer
authentication. See **Receiving data from the Emmy Platform** for verification
details and an example delivery to your agency.

tags.name: Overview
tags.description:
Your agency can receive data from Emmy through webhooks as an alternative to
SFTP, email, or S3 delivery. With webhook delivery, Emmy sends HTTP POST requests
to HTTPS endpoints hosted by your agency, so the received data can be added to
the correct applicant case.

Depending on your integration, your agency can receive:

- **Income Reports (JSON):** structured income and payroll data.
- **CE Activity Reports (JSON):** community engagement activities, including
  employment, education, community service, and work programs.
- **Documents:** income report PDFs and supporting activity documents, sent as
  raw file bytes with their MIME type.

Arrange the delivery methods, receiver URLs, and any additional headers with
the Emmy team during onboarding. Your receiver verifies each request's
signature, processes the report or document, and returns an HTTP response.
The sections below describe the delivery flow, shared signing and retry
behavior, and the payloads your endpoints receive.

tags.name: Report delivery flow
tags.description:
Emmy sends a completed report to your agency's receiver, which verifies the
request signature, saves the report, and returns an HTTP response.

![Report delivery between Emmy and the agency system](api-flow.png)

The diagram shows the income report flow. The CE Activity Report uses your
agency's configured CE receiver URL, illustrated in this reference as
`/api/v1/income-report`, but might be better named for CE as
`/api/v1/ce-report`.

tags.name: Webhook signatures
tags.description:
Emmy signs outbound webhook requests with your agency's API key. Verify the
signature before processing the report. This signing scheme is shared by the
CE Activity Report, Income Report JSON, and PDF document deliveries.

## Signing headers

| Header | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `X-IVAAS-Timestamp` | Unix timestamp the request was signed at. |
| `X-IVAAS-Signature` | HMAC-SHA512 hexdigest of `"<timestamp>:<request body>"`, keyed with the agency's API key. |
| `X-IVAAS-Confirmation-Code` | The report's confirmation code. Sent with CE Activity Reports and document deliveries; omitted from Income Report JSON POSTs. |

Income Report JSON POSTs include `confirmation_code` in the JSON body but do not
send the `X-IVAAS-Confirmation-Code` header. They still include
`X-IVAAS-Timestamp` and `X-IVAAS-Signature`.

Any additional headers the agency requires (for example an API gateway key) can be configured per-agency and are sent verbatim.

Sign the exact bytes sent, including any trailing
newline; reformatting JSON after signing changes the signature.


## Verifying a signature

Compute an HMAC-SHA512 hex digest of the timestamp, a colon, and the exact raw
request body, using your agency's API key. Compare it with `X-IVAAS-Signature`
using a constant-time comparison. Use the `X-IVAAS-Timestamp` header as sent;
do not parse and reserialize the JSON before checking the signature.

## cURL example

Save the request payload shown in the OpenAPI reference as `ce-activity-report.json`.
Set `AGENCY_API_KEY` and `AGENCY_REPORT_URL` for your test receiver before running
this command. It simulates Emmy sending a report to your agency and requires
Bash, cURL, OpenSSL, and jq.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${AGENCY_API_KEY:?Set AGENCY_API_KEY to your test agency API key}"
AGENCY_REPORT_URL="${AGENCY_REPORT_URL:-https://agency.example.org/api/v1/ce-activity-report}"
REPORT_FILE="${REPORT_FILE:-ce-activity-report.json}"

timestamp=$(date +%s)
confirmation_code=$(jq -er '.confirmation_code' "$REPORT_FILE")
signature=$(
  { printf '%s:' "$timestamp"; cat "$REPORT_FILE"; } |
    openssl dgst -sha512 -hmac "$AGENCY_API_KEY" | awk '{print $NF}'
)

curl --request POST "$AGENCY_REPORT_URL" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header "X-IVAAS-Timestamp: $timestamp" \
  --header "X-IVAAS-Signature: $signature" \
  --header "X-IVAAS-Confirmation-Code: $confirmation_code" \
  --data-binary "@$REPORT_FILE"
```

Add any agency-specific gateway headers configured during onboarding. The agency
API key is used for signing; this webhook does not use the invitation API's
`Authorization: Bearer` header.

tags.name: Retry logic
tags.description:
After a failed income report or activity delivery, Emmy retries up to five additional times. The waits
between attempts are 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, and 4 hours.

For combined income JSON and PDF delivery, a PDF retry does not resend the JSON
report when JSON delivery has already succeeded. If the final attempt fails, the job remains failed for investigation by
the Emmy team in partnership with your agency's technical team.

tags.name: CE Activity Reports
tags.description:
Emmy sends completed reports to your agency's systems so they can be added to
the applicant's case. Your agency hosts the receiving endpoint and arranges its
URL and any additional headers during onboarding.

The CE Activity Report webhook below delivers JSON, including income and payroll
data. Its request body describes what your agency receives; its response describes
what your endpoint should return to Emmy. The example agency hostname is a
placeholder. Use your own receiver URL when testing delivery.

tags.name: Income Reports (JSON)
tags.description:
Contact the Emmy Team to request documentation about the Income Report API.

Income Report JSON POSTs include `confirmation_code` in the JSON body, but do
not send the `X-IVAAS-Confirmation-Code` header. The `X-IVAAS-Timestamp` and
`X-IVAAS-Signature` headers are included for signature verification.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description:
This API lets your agency receive documents from the Emmy platform, including
income report PDFs and supporting activity documents.
It is an alternative to other file delivery methods, such as SFTP, S3, or shared
email. Your agency hosts the receiving endpoint and ensures that documents are
added to the correct case in its eligibility management system.

For agencies that also receive income data through the Income Report JSON API,
Emmy sends the PDF after the JSON delivery succeeds.

post.summary: Create a Tokenized Link to Emmy Income
post.description:
Create a personalized income reporting link. Supply `language` (`en` or `es`)
and an `agency_partner_metadata` object using your agency's schema.
The API key determines which agency schema applies; it is not selected by the payload.

The endpoint does not send email or SMS. Deliver the returned link or redirect
the applicant to it. Each request creates a new invitation; there is no
idempotency key or deduplication. Treat tokens as opaque.

This V1 endpoint creates only income invitations. The legacy `activities`
parameter is ignored; it does not create a community engagement invitation.

**Validation:** `422` responses contain field paths and human-readable messages.
Do not depend on exact message wording. Missing metadata or malformed metadata
containers may raise a server error instead of a structured `422`. Always send
`agency_partner_metadata` as an object.

**Origin tracking:** To track where an applicant received a link, append an
`origin` query parameter with a value agreed during onboarding, such as `email`.
Use `?` when the URL has no query string and `&` otherwise.

post.description:
Create a personalized income reporting link and an activity reporting link
for the applicant described by `agency_partner_metadata`. The path segment
`invitation_type` selects which activity flow is created: `employment` or
`community-engagement`.

`verification_range` controls the reporting window for the activity
invitation (`last_complete_month` or `last_12_complete_months`).

post.description:
## Overview

Emmy sends completed reports to your agency's systems so they can be added to
the applicant's case. Your agency hosts the receiving endpoint and arranges its
URL and any additional headers during onboarding.

The CE Activity Report webhook below delivers JSON, including income and payroll
data. Its request body describes what your agency receives; its response describes
what your endpoint should return to Emmy. The example agency hostname is a
placeholder. Use your own receiver URL when testing delivery.

## Model

This document describes the **Community Engagement (CE) Activity Report Transmission API Specification**, a method by which CE activity data can be sent from the Eligibility made easy (Emmy) platform to an agency's systems.

The agency must build an API endpoint that meets this specification and integrates with agency systems to process the activity report into the case file for the correct client.

This revision covers `community_service`, `work_program`, `employment`, and `education`. Employment includes self-attested work and payroll data from linked Argyle or Pinwheel accounts. Education includes self-attested credits, verified NSC enrollment, and partially self-attested education.

## Transmission

Emmy sends a completed CE Activity Report as an HTTP `POST` to an endpoint
hosted by your agency. This is an outbound webhook, not an endpoint on Emmy's
Dev or Demo servers.

### POST /api/v1/ce-activity-report

This API endpoint is built by the agency and receives one CE activity report record. The endpoint URL can be whatever the agency desires, however, it must include a version number to allow for easy upgrades in the future.

The complete `CeActivityReport` model is published in the generated
OpenAPI reference, along with component models for the report,
review period, documents, activity types, and payroll details. Find the webhook
under **Receiving data from the Emmy Platform**. The request example
comes from the tested serializer and includes community service, work programs,
linked payroll, self-employment, unpaid work, and all three education variants.

### Request signatures

See [Webhook signatures](#tag/webhook-signatures) for signing headers,
verification guidance, and a signed cURL example for testing your receiver.

## Response

The agency should respond with `200` and a payload containing:

```json
{
  "status": "received",
  "confirmation_code": "SANDBOX123",
  "received_at": "2026-08-11T14:00:05Z",
  "schema_version_received": "1.0.0",
  "unrecognized_fields_detected": false
}
```

Emmy currently checks the HTTP status and does not validate this response body.

## Request body

The request body uses the `CeActivityReport` OpenAPI model. Expand its properties
and linked models in the reference for field descriptions, required and nullable
fields, monthly reporting rules, and the employment and education variants.
The generated request example shows a complete report with all activity types.

# **Design Principles**

| Design | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| Tolerant Reader | Systems should accept payloads that contain unknown or extra fields without rejecting them. Only a minimal set of fields are truly required. |
| Additive-only schema evolution | New fields can be added to the spec at any time without breaking existing integrations. Fields are only removed in major version releases. |
| Soft required fields | Fields that should be present but may not always be available from upstream providers are not marked as required, and denote `null` as an acceptable value. |

post.description:
The endpoint receives one document per HTTP POST request. `/api/v1/documents` is a
suggested path; your agency can choose another path that includes a version
number. Arrange the receiver URL during onboarding and accept requests only
over HTTPS.

Use the shared [Webhook signatures](#tag/webhook-signatures)
guidance for signing headers, signature verification, and any additional
agency-specific headers. Verify the signature against the exact document bytes
received in the request body.

servers.description: Agency system (replace with your receiver URL)

parameters.name: Content-Type
parameters.description:
MIME type of the document. Any MIME type is supported; income report PDFs use
`application/pdf`.

parameters.name: Content-Length
parameters.description: Size of the document in bytes.

parameters.name: Content-Disposition
parameters.description:
Sent with supporting activity documents as `attachment; filename="<filename>"`
to identify the transmitted file's name. Not sent with income report PDFs.

parameters.name: X-IVAAS-Document-Id
parameters.description:
Sent with supporting activity documents to identify the document, matching its
`document_id` in the CE Activity Report. For example, `DOC-123`. Not sent with
income report PDFs.

parameters.name: X-IVAAS-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix timestamp used when signing the request.

parameters.name: X-IVAAS-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA512 hexdigest of `"<timestamp>:<request body>"`, keyed with the agency API key.

parameters.name: X-IVAAS-Confirmation-Code
parameters.description: Confirmation code of the submitted report.

requestBody.description:
The document is sent as raw bytes in the request body, without a JSON or multipart
wrapper. Any MIME type is supported; `Content-Type` identifies the document
format, such as `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, or `application/octet-stream`.

200.description:
Return `200 OK` when the document has been successfully received by your agency's
system. Emmy uses the HTTP status to determine delivery success and does not
validate the response body. The transmitter accepts any `2xx` success status;
other statuses cause delivery to fail and trigger a retry. See [Retry logic](#tag/retry-logic).

| HTTP status | Meaning | Emmy action |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `200 OK` | The document was successfully received. | Mark delivery successful. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Signature verification failed. | Retry delivery. |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | The receiving system could not process the request. | Retry delivery. |

Use appropriate error statuses, such as `400 Bad Request`, `404 Not Found`,
`408 Request Timeout`, `413 Content Too Large`, `429 Too Many Requests`, or
`502 Bad Gateway`, to help diagnose failed deliveries.

bearerAuth.description: Agency API key. Send Authorization: Bearer API_KEY. The key determines the agency; do not send a client_agency_id.

AgencyPartnerMetadata.description:
Metadata links a submitted report to the agency's records. Select the schema
for the agency associated with your API key. Sandbox and Louisiana have
separate field sets; do not combine them. Some agency schemas overlap, so
matching a schema alone does not identify the agency.

Unrecognized fields and `individual_id` are ignored by this V1 endpoint.
The response contains all accepted fields for the agency, with `null` for
omitted values. Values are echoed as supplied, including date strings.
Supply dates of birth as `MM/DD/YYYY`.

Metadata links a submitted report to the agency's records. Select the schema

separate field sets; do not combine them. Some agency schemas overlap, so

Unrecognized fields and `individual_id` are ignored by this V1 endpoint.
The response contains all accepted fields for the agency, with `null` for
omitted values. Values are echoed as supplied, including date strings.
Supply dates of birth as `MM/DD/YYYY`.

ce_report.description: Community engagement report containing the review period, supporting document metadata, and activities.

CeActivityReport.description:
This document describes the **Community Engagement (CE) Activity Report Transmission API Specification**, a method by which CE activity data can be sent from the Eligibility made easy (Emmy) platform to an agency's systems.

The agency must build an API endpoint that meets this specification and integrates with agency systems to process the activity report into the case file for the correct client.

This revision covers `community_service`, `work_program`, `employment`, and `education`. Employment includes self-attested work and payroll data from linked Argyle or Pinwheel accounts. Education includes self-attested credits, verified NSC enrollment, and partially self-attested education.

report_variant.description: Reporting flow used to complete this report.

review_period.description: Full date range covered by this CE compliance determination, expressed as inclusive calendar months.

documents.description: All supporting documents uploaded for the activities in this report. The files are transmitted separately by the document transmission integration; this array describes what to expect.

activities.description: Activities grouped first by type, then by reporting month in YYYY-MM format.

CeReport.description: The report's review period, supporting documents, and reported activities.

start_month.description: First calendar month of the review period, inclusive, in YYYY-MM format.

end_month.description: Last calendar month of the review period, inclusive, in YYYY-MM format.

CeReviewPeriod.description: Inclusive calendar months covered by the report.

document_id.description: Identifier based on the Emmy Active Storage attachment ID, referenced by an activity's document_ids.

document_name.description: Filename used when transmitting the document separately.

file_type.description: File extension without the leading dot.

CeDocument.description: Metadata for a supporting document. The document itself is transmitted separately.

community_service.description: Map of YYYY-MM calendar months to activity arrays. Months with no reported activity are omitted; no activities is an empty object.

work_program.description: Map of YYYY-MM calendar months to activity arrays. Months with no reported activity are omitted; no activities is an empty object.

employment.description: Map of YYYY-MM calendar months to activity arrays. Months with no reported activity are omitted; no activities is an empty object.

education.description: Map of YYYY-MM calendar months to activity arrays. Months with no reported activity are omitted; no activities is an empty object.

CeActivities.description: Keys are activity types, each containing a map of YYYY-MM months to activity arrays. Months with no reported activity are omitted; an activity type with no activities is an empty object. Activities spanning several months appear under each applicable month.

type.description: Activity type, matching the enclosing activity-type key.

month.description: Calendar month this activity applies to in YYYY-MM format; repeats the enclosing month key.

data_source.description: Origin of the activity data: self_attested for manually reported activities, validated for linked Argyle or Pinwheel payroll, verified for NSC enrollment, or verified_enrollment_only for NSC enrollment with self-attested credits.

document_ids.description: Supporting document_id values from the report's documents array. Empty for linked payroll; self-attested documents are referenced from their own activities.

CeActivity.description: Fields shared by all activity entries in the enclosing reporting month.

street_address.description: Street address of the organization, employer, or school.

street_address_line_2.description: Additional street address information, such as an apartment or suite.

city.description: City of the organization, employer, or school.

CeEmploymentActivity.description: One employer's activity in the enclosing month, either self-attested or validated payroll data. Employment follows the September 4 specification's JSON examples: has_other_jobs and income_summary are omitted, while the CE envelope and review_period are preserved.

CeSelfAttestedEmploymentActivity.description: Published self-attested work appears once per reported month, including months with zero hours or income. Draft activities are excluded. Includes address components, applicant comments, monthly hours, and supporting document IDs. Employer contact details are null for self-employment.

paystubs.description: Only payments dated within the enclosing month and review period. Grouped by pay_date, even when the work period falls in another month. Undated paychecks and paychecks outside the review period are omitted.

CeValidatedEmploymentActivity.description: Only published, successfully synchronized Argyle or Pinwheel accounts are included. Each employer appears once per month with a paycheck in the review period; employers without dated paychecks in that period have no entry. Payroll money values are in cents, and nullable provider fields remain null. Hours are reported on each paystub as hours_paid; there is no calculated employment-level hours field. A failed payroll fetch fails transmission so the job can retry rather than sending a partial report.

CeEducationActivity.description: Only published education activities are included: self-attested credits, verified NSC enrollment, or verified enrollment with self-attested credits. Fully self-attested education appears under each reported month. NSC term entries appear under each applicable reporting month, including eligible summer carryover. A month can contain multiple schools or terms.
